issue.title: Redundant foreign keys during autogenerate

labels.name: external SQLAlchemy issues
labels.description: the issue is in SQLAlchemy, not here in alembic

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
This is somewhat related to #519 except that the table names are in Title case.

Repeated execution of `alembic revision --autogenerate` then `alembic upgrade head` is continuously dropping all the existing foreign keys and regenerating them.

These are the versions:
SQLAlchemy - 1.3.5
Alembic - 1.0.11
MySQL - 5.7
PyMySQL - 0.9.3

```python
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy.schema import Column, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.types import CHAR, VARCHAR

convention = {
  "ix": 'ix_%(column_0_label)s',
  "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
  "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
  "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
  "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s"
}
meta = MetaData(naming_convention=convention)
Base = declarative_base(metadata=meta)

class Table1(Base):
	__tablename__ = "Table1"
	id = Column(CHAR(36), primary_key=True)
	name = Column(VARCHAR(255))

class Table2(Base):
	__tablename__ = "Table2"
	id = Column(CHAR(36), primary_key=True)
	name = Column(VARCHAR(255), unique=True)
	table1_id = Column(CHAR(36), ForeignKey("Table1.id"))
```

I find that it is happening due to mismatch in signature calculation. 

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/f723827c82dfdb1145f3c73a88ad61bda1ca8d7f/alembic/autogenerate/compare.py#L997-L998

At the lines above, here are the signatures in my tests:

For `conn_fk_by_sig`:
`(None, 'Table2', ('table1_id',), None, 'table1', ('id',), None, None, 'not deferrable')`

For `metadata_fks_by_sig`:
`(None, 'Table2', ('table1_id',), None, 'Table1', ('id',), None, None, 'not deferrable')`

Notice that the difference is only in the case of the referred table (`table1` and `Table1`). 

When I edited [the class](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/f723827c82dfdb1145f3c73a88ad61bda1ca8d7f/alembic/autogenerate/compare.py#L384)(`_fk_constraint_sig`) to convert all referred table names to lowercase, it worked fine.

How can I fix this?

body:
I have a mysql 8 running on a container with lower case FS and lower_case_table_names=2.

The issue described in https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=88718 does not exist; the column name is in the correct case.  However, the table name is not:

```
MySQL [test]> CREATE TABLE `Table_One` (
    ->   `Id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
    -> );
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.058 sec)

MySQL [test]> 
MySQL [test]> CREATE TABLE `table_two` (
    ->   `TABLE_ONE_ID` INTEGER,
    ->   FOREIGN KEY (`TABLE_ONE_ID`) REFERENCES `Table_One` (`Id`)
    -> );
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.082 sec)

MySQL [test]> 
MySQL [test]> SHOW CREATE TABLE `table_two`;
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table     | Create Table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| table_two | CREATE TABLE `table_two` (
  `TABLE_ONE_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  KEY `TABLE_ONE_ID` (`TABLE_ONE_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `table_two_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`TABLE_ONE_ID`) REFERENCES `table_one` (`Id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.001 sec)

```

so...the 88718 fix has nothing to do with this, this is...another MySQL issue as far as I can tell at the moment

rename.from: very possible that lower_case_table_names=2 doesn't work with _correct_for_mysql_bug_88718
rename.to: need an 88718-style workaround for table names

body:
**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Correct for MySQL 8.0 table and schema names in FK reflection** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1381

issue.title: Added upper bound to mysql version needing bugfix correction
issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->
Provided an update to self._needs_correct_for_88718_96365, adding 8.0.13 as the highest mysql version requiring this correction. Follow up to https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4751

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->
https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=88718 was fixed in MySQL 8.0.14, so updating the check to reflect that.
When running the tests against a db running in a mysql:8.0.13 docker image, the tests pass, but if the upper limit is set to exclude 8.0.13 from using the correction, test_correct_for_mysql_bugs_88718_96365 and test_case_sensitive_column_constraint_reflection in test_reflection.py fail (as expected). When setting the upper limit to the correct 8.0.13, all of the reflection tests pass against mysql:8.0.12, mysql:8.0.13, mysql:8.0.14, and mysql:latest.

I am a bit confused, though, as it looks like https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=96365 was active as of at least mysql 8.0.17, but I am unable to reproduce in 8.0.14 and would like some clarity on that part.
Here's what I get using 8.0.14.
```sql
CREATE TABLE `Table_One` (
 `Id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY );
 
 CREATE TABLE `table_two` (`TABLE_ONE_ID` INTEGER, FOREIGN KEY (`TABLE_ONE_ID`) REFERENCES `Table_One` (`Id`) );
 
 SHOW CREATE TABLE `table_two`;
'CREATE TABLE `table_two` (
  `TABLE_ONE_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  KEY `TABLE_ONE_ID` (`TABLE_ONE_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `table_two_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`TABLE_ONE_ID`) REFERENCES **`Table_One`** (`Id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci'
```
This looks correct, unlike the output in the bug report, which was:
```sql
CREATE TABLE `table_two` (
  `TABLE_ONE_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  KEY `TABLE_ONE_ID` (`TABLE_ONE_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `table_two_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`TABLE_ONE_ID`) REFERENCES **`table_one`** (`Id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
```
Please let me know if there are any other steps to test/reproduce this.
